title: Looking at how big studios use AI
author: katatonicmango
selftext:
I looked into some games from bigger studios that have used AI and found an interesting quote from November of last year. Nexon CEO Junghun Lee said, "It's important to assume that every game company is now using AI." 

  
That's kinda how I think of things, but it's interesting to see what people get outraged over. I was bummed by the backlash of Big Walk when CoD's AI disclosure doesn't get as much attention. The witch hunts will just encourage devs to be more vague or even lie about AI use instead of being open which helps to normalize it. 

  
I also find it interesting how the Steam disclosure splits things. Are some people against pre-generated AI content but totally fine with live-generated AI content?

Curious to hear what you guys think.

I made a video walking through ten games if you are interested: [https://youtu.be/DVQEo8vf5V0](https://youtu.be/DVQEo8vf5V0)

comments.author: R_dva
comments.body:
I worked at a company that developed AAA game, if it possible even call this particular game a "AAA" game and they had a special, hidden repository containing a whole bunch of pirated software.

knowing them, they definitely will use AI in any field, code, art and so

replies.author: katatonicmango
replies.body: Woah that's super interesting. I mean when I think of AAA I assume they have everything down to a formula to try and make the most money, not just when it comes to workflow but also writing and even art style. That's why I'm excited for indie devs to use AI because at least they have new voices with new ideas rather than churning out what they think will make money.
